title: Pilot runway governance & cost sprint - AetherWorks QBR
summary: Quarterly health check focused on pilot runway, governance controls for Private deployment, and a short cost-sprint plan. Discussed current usage patterns (spikes on inference), early reliability incidents, upcoming model rollouts, and a proposed 6-week cost/reliability sprint. Agreed action items: Redwood to share scoped price sheet and security pack, AetherWorks to provide sample traffic traces and SLO targets, and schedule a 2-hour benchmarking window for latency/cost verification.
topics: Usage patterns and burst spikes (weekend batch vs realtime)
Cost profile breakdown and optimization levers (quant, batching, cache)
Private deployment governance: KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML and RBAC specifics
Reliability incidents and mitigation: autoscale thresholds and fallback policies
Pilot scope and 6-week cost/reliability sprint plan
Next steps: benchmarks, pricing, security docs
action_items: Jamie Ortega - Share detailed pilot pricing sheet and model-specific unit costs - 2027-04-04
Ravi Patel - Prepare benchmark run plan and measurement script; include KV cache and batching toggles - 2027-04-06
Lina Gomez - Upload 72 hours of representative traffic traces and SLO definitions to shared drive - 2027-04-05
Priya Nair - Compile list of compliance questions and KMS configuration preferences; share firewall/VPC diagram - 2027-04-07
Daniel Cho - Provide current monthly inference spend and top 3 cost drivers (by route/model) - 2027-04-08
next_steps: Redwood to send pilot contract template and pricing worksheet (by 2027-04-04)
Schedule 2-hour benchmark window w/ AetherWorks -- propose 2027-04-12-13 slots
Redwood SE to run preliminary stress tests in staging and share results
Customer to confirm SSO/SAML metadata for Private deploy trial
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-01 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Ortega (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (AetherWorks Head of ML), Markus Lee (VP Eng), Priya Nair (Cloud Security), Daniel Cho (FinOps)

Auto-generated Summary: (may be rough) - pilot scope, cost sprint, security pack request, and benchmark window.

---
[00:00] Jamie Ortega: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining on a Friday afternoon, appreciate it. Quick roll call — I'll be jamie, ravi with me on the SE side. Lina, Markus, Priya, Daniel, you there?
[00:06] Lina Gomez: yep yep, hi jamie, hey ravi, all good here.
[00:08] Markus Lee: here. Sorry I was on another thread, joined.
[00:10] Priya Nair: hi.
[00:11] Daniel Cho: hi all.

[00:15] Jamie Ortega: great. Objective for today — short QBR/checkin: usage trends, cost signals, a couple of reliability blips you saw last month, and then a proposed 6-week cost and reliability sprint to tighten the pilot runway. we'll also touch on governance for the Private pilot — KMS, audit logs, SSO. Sound okay?
[00:30] Lina Gomez: yeah sounds good. We've got some internal stake holders listening but wanted to get aligned so thanks.

[00:45] Ravi Patel: i'll give the technical read after jamie and then we can dive into the benchmarking plan.

---
Section: Usage & Cost Notes
[01:02] Lina Gomez: quick context — since onboarding in feb we've got two main traffic modes: scheduled batch enrichment overnight and realtime routes during business hours. The realtime route has been growing, and two weekends ago we saw a burst where latency spiked. That is what triggered the alerting.
[01:22] Jamie Ortega: got it, and do you recall if that burst correlates to a model rollout or a promo/traffic campaign?
[01:28] Lina Gomez: we had a minor model update — not a big architecture change — but it was coupled with a marketing email that drove more lookups. So a little bit of both.
[01:40] Daniel Cho: from finance, last month inference costs were ~1.9x what we expected, main drivers were peak token counts on that realtime route and some repeated small requests that didn't benefit from caching.
[01:55] Markus Lee: the small requests are microfront-end calls from the mobile client — we didn't batch them yet server-side.
[02:06] Ravi Patel: okay two levers here: batching (client-side or server middleware) and prefix/KV cache. If we can autocache repeated prefixes and tune batch sizes we usually get big wins, but it trades off latency for small requests.
[02:26] Lina Gomez: we care about p95 latency under 180ms for the realtime route, otherwise product teams push back.
[02:34] Jamie Ortega: okay that's a clear SLO to aim for. We'll treat that as a constraint in the cost sprint.

---
Section: Reliability incidents and fallbacks
[02:50] Priya Nair: from security/ops — we saw a failed container restart in the dedicated staging pool and an autoscale misfire. the logs had a kv-cache mount error — i think it was a mounting timing issue.
[03:06] Ravi Patel: yeah, mounting timing on the NFS/kv is a known-flaky thing in some cloud setups; in production we recommend our managed prefix cache or sticky routing to healthy nodes. Also the fallback policy we discussed last quarter (auto-fallback to a smaller unquantized variant) wasn't enabled on that route.
[03:26] Markus Lee: right, fallback wasn't enabled — we kept it off because we were worried about quality variance.
[03:34] Lina Gomez: quality matters, but we can tolerate a shorter context fallback if it keeps the app online.
[03:42] Jamie Ortega: good trade — we can do a canary policy: enable fallback to a trimmed context model for 5% of traffic during the spike window. monitor hallucination/regression metrics.

---
Section: Governance & Private deployment specifics
[04:05] Priya Nair: two governance questions: 1) KMS integration — we prefer our HSM-backed KMS, need to confirm Redwood can integrate with external key providers; 2) audit logs and retention: we need 2 years of immutable logs for compliance.
[04:21] Jamie Ortega: quick answers — yes we support external KMS/HSM integrations for Private, we have an integration guide; audit logs are supported and retention is configurable — we should align on the exact schemas for immutable event logs. i'll send the security pack with examples.
[04:37] Priya Nair: also SSO/SAML — we need RBAC mappings and SCIM for groups.
[04:44] Ravi Patel: scim and SAML are supported, and for the pilot we can pre-provision admin dev and read-only roles. We'll map groups to roles.
[04:55] Priya Nair: perfect. Please include firewall requirements — egress IPs, etc.

---
Section: Cost optimization levers discussed
[05:10] Jamie Ortega: high-level levers we recommend: 1) quantization profiles (FP16/INT8 where acceptable), 2) batching and continuous batching thresholds, 3) prefix/KV caching for repeated tokens, 4) routing policies to cheaper variants during non-critical windows, 5) model-surgery — smaller distilled models for specific routes.
[05:32] Daniel Cho: curious about quantization — how much do we realistically save vs latency diff? we don't want to regress quality.
[05:40] Ravi Patel: in our experience INT8 can reduce cost ~2x for generation with small latency improvement on modern kernels, but there's a quality trade. Our Optimize tool can run A/B evals against your prompts. For the pilot we'll run a few prompts in the bench to estimate quality delta.
[05:58] Lina Gomez: okay let's make the bench include our top 50 production prompts.

---
Section: Pilot/runway proposal (6-week sprint)
[06:10] Jamie Ortega: proposed plan: week 0 - agreement on SLOs and data; week 1-2 - bench runs and canary config tests; week 3-4 - enable caching/batching/quant on staging and measure; week 5-6 - controlled prod ramp for the optimizations + governance signoff. deliverables: cost delta estimates and an ops runbook.
[06:33] Markus Lee: that timeline is workable. We want a hard safety rollback mechanism and feature flags.
[06:39] Ravi Patel: we can ship rollout hooks and automatic fallback to a safe model variant. We'll also provide tracing hooks for per-request token breakdown.

---
[07:02] Lina Gomez: quick question, the bench—will that simulate weekend spikes too? we want to include batch+realtime mixed workload.
[07:08] Ravi Patel: yes we can create a mixed workload scenario with burst patterns and measure both tail latency and cost per 1k tokens.
[07:18] Daniel Cho: on pricing — is there an easy delta for Dedicated reserved capacity vs hosted per-token? we may move to dedicated if sustained throughput justifies it.
[07:26] Jamie Ortega: we'll share a pricing worksheet. generally Dedicated has a committed capacity model that reduces unit costs at scale, but dedicated also has minimum commitments and setup. The worksheet will show break-even points given your 3-month forecast.

---
Section: Compliance and procurement notes
[07:45] Priya Nair: procurement will need SOC2 docs, certs, and an SLA for the dedicated pilot. Also want to confirm data residency options if we ever host in eu/uk.
[07:55] Jamie Ortega: we have SOC2 reports and a standard enterprise SLA. For data residency, Private can be deployed into your VPC/region; we'll include that in the security pack.
[08:05] Priya Nair: ok please attach the latest cert.

---
Section: Open questions (customer)
[08:12] Markus Lee: two things — 1) what's the expected time to spin a Private pilot? 2) how intrusive is schema-level logging for PII?
[08:21] Jamie Ortega: Private pilot spin up time depends on access: if we have infra creds and SSO metadata it can be 2-3 weeks for a minimal setup; full production-grade with HA and HSM can be longer. On PII: audit logs can be redacted at schema level, and we support token-level masking. We'll need to align on retention policies.
[08:40] Lina Gomez: ok that's fine. 2-3 weeks sounds reasonable.

---
Section: Quick live walkthrough (Ravi)
[08:55] Ravi Patel: (screen share noise) so here's a quick tracing view — token breakdown by route, per-token cost line items, fallback flags. sorry some of the labels look off on this exported CSV, fireflies transcribed 'kv-cache' as 'key-cash' — hah.
[09:12] Lina Gomez: lol yes i noticed some of the transcript typos earlier.
[09:15] Ravi Patel: bottom line, we can toggle prefix cache, change batch window from 8ms to 30ms and observe throughput vs p95. We can also test INT8 vs FP16 in the same bench run.

---
Section: Recap and commitments
[09:40] Jamie Ortega: recap — Redwood will: 1) send pilot pricing sheet and contract template; 2) send security pack with KMS/HSM guide, SOC2 and audit schema examples; 3) SE will deliver the bench plan and proposed slots for 2-hour run; 4) provide initial projection of break-even for Dedicated. Customer will: 1) share 72 hours of traffic traces and SLOs, 2) provide SSO metadata and VPC diagram, 3) give procurement contact for certs.
[10:05] Lina Gomez: yep that's accurate. We should set a checkpoint after bench results to decide whether to enable quant on the realtime route.
[10:12] Jamie Ortega: agreed — we'll include decision gates in the runbook.
[10:18] Daniel Cho: finance will review pricing sheet and produce a 3-month forecast; i'll push that to the shared drive.
[10:25] Priya Nair: i'll collate security questions asap.

---
Closing
[10:35] Jamie Ortega: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the artifact bundle and calendar invites. Any last questions?
[10:41] Markus Lee: no, thanks — appreciate the pragmatic plan.
[10:43] Lina Gomez: thanks all.
[10:45] Ravi Patel: thanks. Bye.
[10:48] (call ends)
